steps.text: Prepare a skillet with cooking spray and place over medium-high heat.
Whisk together the muffin mix, flour, baking powder, egg, milk, and cooking oil until smooth.

Pour 1/4 cup of batter into skillet. Cook pancake until bubbles form on top and bottom is golden brown, 1 to 2 minutes; flip and cook until bottom side reaches same golden-brown color of top of pancake. Repeat until batter is completely used.

raw_recipe.headline: Corn Muffin Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: Quickly whip together a pancake batter with prepared muffin mix, flour, baking powder, egg, and milk.

review.reviewBody: This is Heather, the creator of this recipe. As a suggestion for others when using this recipe, I have substituted the corn muffin with apple cinnamon muffin mix, berrry muffin mix, and bannana nut muffin mix. That is actually my daughter's preferred way of eatting them. Any style muffin mix will do. I hope you all enjoy it.

Good recipe but mine were more pancake than cornbread. I added 1/4c of milk to offset the extra 1.5oz in Jiffy mix. Also lost 1 to a way too hot pan... I recommend medium heat vs med-high. 

Next time I will substitute buttermilk for milk and ghee (butter) for oil. I will also use 1/4c of whole wheat flour instead of more milk and cook in a cast iron skillet to better control heat.

All around good basic recipe to start from. Look forward to making with changes and may try with other mixes too.

This was horrible! Is this recipe really supposed to have 2 TABLESPOONS of baking powder? I followed the recipe exactly as written & my family & I couldn’t eat the pancakes. There was a weird taste & kind of hot sensation in our mouth from eating a few of them. I thought it seemed weird that it was tablespoons & not teaspoons of baking powder, but I did not see any other review mentioning this, so I continued with the recipe. I tripled the recipe because my kids love pancakes & I had to throw the batter & pancakes away. So disappointing.
*After looking further at the other reviews, I saw two people had changed their recipe from tablespoons to teaspoons. Ugh! I wish I would’ve looked at more reviews or trusted my instinct on the measurements. 
This recipe needs to be edited.
I used 2 tsp instead of tablespoons of baking powder. I used the whole larger package of Jiffy and just added milk till I looked the consistency of the badder.

I added 1/4 cup sour cream to add more moisture, texture and flavor. I can only eat 1 at a time so I cook and refrigerate the others to warm in the toaster at a later time. They make a great middle of the day snack!
I substituted pancake mix for the flour and baking powder, I added sautéed bananas and ssprinkled cinnamon into the batter. I also stirred in some honey..... Yum but sticky on the pan.

My 7 year old daughter did the measuring and mixing for me. We used a Pumpkin muffin mix from Aldi that was 14oz rather then 7oz. I had her do the conversions to double the other ingredients. I also had her add in chopped walnuts. I will freeze the extras to reheat later this week. My daughter thought it was so cool that we were using the muffin mix to make pancakes. She's been making muffins, cupcakes and brownies from box mixes so this was a non-intimidating way to have her move into making things with more ingredients. Then all I have to do is the baking. I didn't read the reviews before hanb and didn't even think about the baking powder being too much. I will definitely only use 2 tsp next time we make these. I did also add more milk to make it the right consistency for pouring. I assume this varies to some degree depending on the muffin mix that is used. These were light, fluffy and yummy! This would be an easy recipe to use for jar gifts at Christmas.

The whole purpose of me wanting to use jiffy mix to make pancakes was because I ran out of baking powder and did not want to make the trip to the grocery store this morning so I improvised. I used one teaspoon of baking soda, I also used buttermilk instead of regular milk and I added a tablespoon of vanilla extract. They were awesome!

Using the whole 8.5 oz Jiffy Mix: 2 eggs, 1 TBSP baking soda, 1 and 1/4 cup flour, 1 tsp of salt, 1 TBSP of sugar. (Eggs and flour help it hold together better, salt and sugar help with the baking soda taste, might even want to try a little vanilla extract).
If I could give this zero stars, I would. These are inedible with 2 Tbs. of baking powder. It’s disgusting.

I have been trying to re-create a corn cake like the ones at a favorite Minneapolis restaurant that is due to close and this is the third one I tried and it's the closest to their corncake.
Next time, I think I should add a little salt and fresher baking powder.

I love this recipe. My dad used to make regular pancakes with whole kernel corn. This was good eating. The corn added sweetness and texture. Limited corn, not enough to replace the pancakes, but I don't have or remember the recipe. This would be a popular recipe imho. Thank you in advance.
Too much baking powder, too little milk, these are nothing like north eastern johnny cakes all around bad texture
I added strawberries, granola, and 1/4 cup flour. These were so tasty. My little girl and I had fun making them. And they taste like my Mama's pancakes. Thank you so much for this recipe. ❤️👩‍👧
wasted pancakes!! I used what the recipe said which was 2 tablespoons of baking soda and it is inedible!!

I should have measured the ingredients more carefully because the batter is too thick. I should try more milk to make it easier to scoop the batter into the skillet and to not havexthem crumble apart when they are flipped over. I wonder about trying the mixture into my Belgian waffle maker. I think I might try it. The taste of the pancakes is really yummy.

I followed the recipe, exactly as written. Did not turn out well... Tasted of baking powder and didn’t stay together well. The only plus was a fluffy texture, but because the pancakes completely fell apart, it was hard to get the texture from the crumbly mess. Will not make again.
Delicious. Super simple. Everyone loved them.
This was easy and very tasty. I did use the jiffy mix which is 8.5 ounces and the pancakes seemed to fall apart so next time I’ll adjust the Ingredients accordingly. But they were very tasty
My husband loved these pancakes! The only thing was that they fell apart easily.
